exemptions.reason: Like Datastore, Firestore documents are Value unions, and the REST surface uses the recursive {+parent} document path. A like-for-like comparison needs a projection; tracked as AUD3-3.

The object/bucket surface needs the media-upload flow, and the official Go client module does not export the storage v2 proto the emulator serves (the gRPC conformance suite uses the emulator's own storagepb), so a raw cross-transport body diff needs its own harness work. Tracked as AUD3-4.
REST is the legacy v1 project shape while the proto is v3 (the deliberate v1/v3 alignment from the dual-protocol effort), so a full-body diff needs a logical projection. Tracked as AUD3-5.

The gRPC surface is the shared google.iam.v1.IAMPolicy service while REST iam is service-account admin plus a resource policy; a like-for-like comparison needs a shared policy target. Tracked as AUD3-6.
IAM Credentials exposes only GenerateAccessToken/GenerateIdToken (no resource lifecycle) and the tokens are volatile; a create/get/list/delete parity flow does not apply. Tracked as AUD3-7.
Dataproc cluster/job resources carry a heavier model and region-scoped paths; the parity flow needs LRO handling plus a cluster fixture. Tracked as AUD3-8.
GKE cluster mutations return the container-specific google.container.v1.Operation (not google.longrunning), and a cluster fixture needs a node-pool model. Tracked as AUD3-9.
An execution requires a deployed Workflow prerequisite and an execution lifecycle; the flow needs REST prerequisite setup. Tracked as AUD3-10.
